answer: A harbor can resist fake fleets by giving every identity custody of one unique data shard: to register, an agent must store a distinct shard of a public archive and serve random audit reads, like a sonnet that only makes sense when every line is present. Audits strike many identities at the same instant, so one disk cannot answer for a thousand — each extra identity needs its own storage and bandwidth, a spiral of cost that grows linearly and cannot be shared, faked, or amortized by faster compute.
